headline: Chip-sector selloff drags S&P 500 and Nasdaq lower in overnight trade as the Fed's two-day meeting opens and US-Iran de-escalation talks pull oil off recent highs.
stance: The setup is binary today: the FOMC begins its July 28-29 meeting with markets split — a hold is the consensus, but a non-trivial minority price in a hike by September, and Chair Warsh has pledged zero forward guidance. Asian chip stocks cratered overnight (South Korea's Kospi fell ~9%, Japan's Nikkei ~4%), pressuring US semiconductor names and pulling equity futures lower. The one relief valve is oil: Trump's comments on US-Iran talks sent crude below Monday's cash close, which helps the inflation narrative and modestly steadies bonds.

news.head: Fed meeting day-1 — hold expected, hike risk alive
news.body: The FOMC convenes today; consensus is a hold at 3.50–3.75%, but roughly 36% of futures contracts price a hike at some point near-term, and the June dot-plot showed nine of eighteen officials favoring at least one increase this year — Warsh's press conference tomorrow is the main event.

news.head: Chip stocks in freefall — AI capex doubts spread to Asia
news.body: Overnight, SK Hynix fell as much as 13% and Samsung up to 10%, dragging the Kospi down ~9% — mounting doubt over whether hyperscaler AI spending can justify the memory-chip investment cycle is the common thread.

news.head: US-Iran talks — oil retreats, bonds rally
news.body: Trump said the US and Iran are engaged in active talks to end the Middle East conflict; oil extended a steep decline on the news, and Treasury bonds extended gains as the energy-driven inflation premium eased.

news.head: Megacap earnings gauntlet starts Wednesday
news.body: Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft all report Wednesday-Thursday; Alphabet's prior-week beat-but-spend-scare set a high bar — investors want revenue beats paired with capex discipline, not the reverse.

news.head: SpaceX now 51% off its post-IPO high
news.body: SpaceX shares, which IPO'd at $135 on June 12, were trading around $109 Monday — more than 51% below the all-time high of $225.64 — marking the tenth negative session in twelve.

implications: Equity futures are tracking lower in the overnight session (S&P 500 cash closed at 7,413.18 Mon; pre-market CFD ~7,400) — chip weakness is the single biggest drag, and it can spread into data-center names before the open.
Bond yields eased overnight as oil fell; the 10-year closed at 4.65% Monday — any further oil decline keeps that bid alive, but a hawkish Warsh tone Wednesday could reverse it fast.
The yen (prior cash close 163.70 ¥/$) sits at a 3-year extreme — Bank of Japan intervention risk is live at these levels; a sharp yen move would ripple through global risk assets.

Positioning: Speculators in S&P 500 futures are extended long (85th percentile of 3-year positioning) — a contrarian warning for large-caps. Russell 2000 specs are at the opposite extreme with almost no bullish bets left — a contrarian floor for small-caps. In rates, speculators have almost no bullish bets left in 3M SOFR (4th percentile) — also a contrarian floor, consistent with a market that is over-pricing hike risk. In commodities, Copper specs are heavily positioned long (96th percentile) — a contrarian warning given copper already trades at an extreme 3-year high of $6.40/lb.

watch.head: FOMC statement — 2 pm ET Wednesday
watch.body: No dot-plot this meeting — the policy statement wording and any dissenting votes are the only official signal; Warsh has pledged minimal forward guidance, so any surprise language moves rates and equities fast.

watch.head: Semiconductor cascade — can SMH stabilize?
watch.body: The VanEck Semiconductor ETF lost more than 2% Monday on top of prior-week losses; watch for a pre-market stabilization or further selling — the level sets the tone for tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 futures.

watch.head: Oil vs. inflation trade-off
watch.body: WTI (prior cash close $81.91/bbl) is falling on Iran-deal talk — every $5 drop in crude mechanically reduces the near-term CPI print and gives the Fed room to stay on hold; watch for any headline that reverses the ceasefire mood.

watch.head: JPY — intervention watch
watch.body: USDJPY at 163.70 (prior cash close) sits at a 99.7th percentile 3-year extreme; the Bank of Japan has intervened at these levels before — a sudden yen strength burst would compress dollar assets globally.

sections.title: Macro & Rates
bullets: 10-year Treasury yield: 4.65% (prior cash close) — bonds caught a modest overnight bid as oil fell on US-Iran de-escalation talks; real yield (inflation-adjusted) sits at 2.44%, still punishing for rate-sensitive assets.

2-year Treasury yield: 4.31% (prior cash close); yield curve (2s-10s) is +34 bps — mildly positive slope signals no immediate recession signal, but the curve could steepen further if the Fed stays on hold and the long end stays anchored.

10-year breakeven inflation (the bond market's inflation forecast): 2.21% (prior cash close) — below the Fed's worry zone for now, but oil's July surge (~20% month-to-date into last week) threatens to push this higher.
FOMC meeting day-1: consensus holds at 3.50–3.75%; futures price roughly a 36% chance of a near-term hike; Chair Warsh explicitly offers no forward guidance — the statement tomorrow is the only read.

Fed balance sheet growing just 1.35% year-over-year; bank reserves $3,062bn; overnight reverse-repo (a measure of excess cash parked at the Fed) at just $1.4bn — system liquidity is ample but not flush.
Term premium (extra yield investors demand for holding long bonds instead of rolling short ones) is 77.9 bps — elevated, reflecting fiscal uncertainty and the ongoing US-Iran conflict cost.
sections.positioning: Speculators have almost no bullish bets left in 3M SOFR futures (4th percentile 3-year range) — a contrarian floor suggesting the market may be over-pricing rate-hike risk at the short end.

sections.title: Equity Markets
bullets: S&P 500: 7,413.18 (prior Mon cash close, +0.02%); overnight pre-market CFD tracking near 7,400 — essentially flat after a mixed Monday where Dow outperformed and Nasdaq lagged.

Nasdaq 100: 24,932.08 (prior Mon cash close, -0.18%); chip-stock weakness overnight in Asia risks an extension at the open — AMD fell 5%, Nvidia 5%, Micron ~2% Monday, and the damage continues overnight in Seoul and Tokyo.
Dow: 52,210.08 (prior Mon cash close, +0.51%) — led by Salesforce (+5.4%), 3M (+3.2%), Sherwin-Williams (+3.1%); the Dow's defensive/industrial tilt is buffering it from the tech selloff.

Breadth: 63.4% of S&P 500 stocks trade above their 50-day average; 66.3% above their 200-day — healthy but not overbought at the index level; Nasdaq breadth is narrower (42.6% above 50-day), confirming the mega-cap concentration risk.

VIX (fear gauge): 18.67 (prior cash close) — calm by historical norms, but the VXN (Nasdaq-specific fear gauge) is elevated at 28.65, reflecting chip/tech uncertainty; SKEW at 146.6 signals options traders are buying tail-risk protection.

CAPE (Shiller price-to-earnings ratio, a long-run valuation measure): 40.47 — near historic highs; equity risk premium (the extra return stocks offer over bonds) is -2%, meaning bonds offer better risk-adjusted value than equities at current levels.

S&P 500 Q2 earnings growth tracking +38% year-over-year per estimates — robust, but the Alphabet post-earnings selloff (beat revenue, spooked on capex) shows the market is penalizing AI spending, not rewarding it.
sections.positioning: Speculators in S&P 500 futures are extended long (85th percentile of 3-year positioning) — a contrarian warning. Russell 2000 specs are at the opposite extreme — almost no bullish bets left (4th percentile) — a contrarian floor for small-caps that could catch a bid if the Fed hold is confirmed.

single_name.note: Five Star Bancorp (community bank) — 2 insider buying rules fired, stock above its 200-day moving line, short interest at 5.7 days-to-cover (shorts are heavy relative to daily volume, creating squeeze risk if buying accelerates); dark-pool and options flow both live. A hold from the Fed tomorrow removes near-term rate-hike risk for regional lenders.

sections.title: Credit & Liquidity
bullets: High-yield credit spread (extra yield junk bonds pay over Treasuries): 279 bps (as of Jul 24) — elevated but not in stress territory; investment-grade spreads at 80 bps also benign; both suggest credit markets are not yet pricing a recession.
HY/IG ETF ratio: 1.3436 (prior cash close) — the relative price of junk-bond ETFs vs. investment-grade is stable, meaning credit investors are not rotating defensively yet.

FRA-OIS and SOFR-OIS spreads (measures of bank funding stress, how much banks charge each other above the risk-free rate): both at just 1 bp — interbank funding is clean; no 2018/2019-style plumbing stress.
Commercial paper spread (short-term corporate funding cost above the risk-free rate): 18 bps — low, confirming short-term credit conditions are easy for corporations.
Bank credit growing +6.4% year-over-year; M2 money supply +5.58% year-over-year — money is growing faster than inflation target, which is one reason the Fed's hawks favor staying restrictive.

4-week moving average of initial jobless claims: 208K (as of Jul 18); single-week claims: 187K — very low, the labor market is not cracking; this removes one argument for a Fed cut and keeps the hike-risk debate live.
